props.title: Scared to Death
props.initialSlug: Teen psychic hunts killer with telekinetic powers

sections.content: **Scared to Death** (1980) represents a fascinating entry in the low-budget horror scene of the early 1980s, arriving just as slasher films like **Friday the 13th** (1980) were taking over theaters. This independent creature feature, directed by William Malone, draws clear inspiration from **Alien** (1979) with its monster design and claustrophobic atmosphere. Malone, who would later direct **House on Haunted Hill** (1999), crafted this cult curiosity on a shoestring budget, featuring a mutant creature terrorizing Los Angeles and a detective trying to stop it.

sections.content: The film's practical effects, while limited by budget constraints, showcase the DIY ingenuity common in horror films of this era. The creature design by Robert Short deserves special mention, predating his later work on **Beetlejuice** (1988). Like contemporary low-budget horror films **The Boogens** (1981) and The Being (1983), Scared to Death demonstrates how regional filmmakers adapted bigger-budget horror concepts for the drive-in and early video market.

The film's structure follows the monster movie playbook established by **Jaws** (1975), keeping the creature hidden for much of the runtime. This technique, born of necessity due to budget limitations, actually works in the film's favor, building tension through suggestion rather than explicit gore. The Los Angeles setting provides an urban backdrop that contrasts with the rural settings common in contemporary horror films like **The Hills Have Eyes** (1977). sections.content: While not a commercial success upon release, **Scared to Death** (1980) exemplifies the ambitious spirit of independent horror filmmaking in the early 1980s. Director William Malone would take lessons learned here into television, directing episodes of **Tales from the Crypt** (1989-1996) and **Freddy's Nightmares** (1988-1990). The film's blend of detective noir and monster movie elements presaged later hybrid genres like **Cast a Deadly Spell** (1991) and **The Hidden** (1987).
